title: Bound browser WebSocket frame size against an unauthenticated memory DoS

claims.statement: Claude Code (claude-code) is the source-producing agent for CHG-0067 under human principal @rodrigoteamx, on the 2026-08-24 directive 'dale al merge y la pasada de hardening' — the first fix from a hardening audit. This does not authorize automatic merge of CHG-0067.
claims.evidence: AGENTS.md, profile.json actors and the 2026-08-24 user directive.

claims.statement: A hardening audit (six adversarial finders over the device-credential, output/WebSocket, production-command, auth/session/CORS, input-validation, and secrets/resources/DoS surfaces, each finding independently verified) confirmed thirteen findings: one high — the browser /ws server sets no maxPayload so an unauthenticated peer can force ~100 MiB frame buffering plus JSON.parse; five medium — the signing DB file is world-readable during and after a failed init, Studio /ws sockets survive logout and session expiry, the session cookie is not Secure under default COOKIE_SECURE='auto' with unset TRUST_PROXY, unbounded element nesting can stack-overflow validation, and ChannelManager.lastActivity grows without eviction; seven low — timing side channels revealing a credential-id and the owner email, the /ws Origin allowlist skipped when the header is absent, de-escalation not tearing down Studio subscriptions, two production idempotency replay gaps, and scene-activate leaking an internal error string.
claims.evidence: The hardening-audit workflow result of 2026-08-24 (13 confirmed, 1 refuted) and the cited source files.

claims.statement: CHG-0067 fixes only the high finding: the browser /ws server is created through createBrowserWebSocketServer() which sets maxPayload to BROWSER_WS_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES (10 MiB, matching the express.json body limit), so ws rejects an over-limit frame with close 1009 before buffering or parsing it — the device gateway already bounds its own frames to 16 KiB. The remaining twelve findings are recorded here and left to successor slices.

Governed discovery reordered the hardening pass to fix the single high-severity, unauthenticated, pre-auth DoS first as a tight low-risk slice, before the medium and low findings, because it is reachable without any credential and denies service to all clients.
claims.evidence: The audit severity ranking and the pre-authentication reachability of the /ws frame handler.

claims.statement: Creating the browser /ws server through a factory that sets a finite maxPayload below the ws default, and proving an over-limit frame is rejected with close 1009 and never delivered, closes the unauthenticated frame-buffering DoS.
claims.evidence: server/tests/unit/browserWebSocketMaxPayload.test.ts asserts the factory's bound and that an oversized frame closes 1009 without delivery.

claims.statement: This slice bounds per-frame size only; it does not add a /ws upgrade or connection rate limit (the express-rate-limit middleware covers /api only), which remains a recorded hardening item.
claims.evidence: server/src/index.ts wsServer upgrade path has no rate limit; the audit's DoS finding also noted the missing throttle.

claims.statement: Human review accepted CHG-0067: the browser /ws server bounds inbound frame size (createBrowserWebSocketServer maxPayload = 10 MiB), so an unauthenticated peer can no longer force ~100 MiB frame buffering and JSON.parse; an oversized frame is rejected with close 1009 without delivery. This is the first fix from a 13-finding hardening audit; the twelve remaining findings stay tracked as frontier hardening nodes.
claims.evidence: server/src/handlers/websocket.ts, server/src/index.ts, server/tests/unit/browserWebSocketMaxPayload.test.ts, the passing full server suite under npm run check, the CHG-0067 pull-request Constitution run (8 jobs green), and human acceptance on 2026-08-24.

claims.statement: The twelve remaining audit findings (signing-file permissions, Studio /ws session revocation, cookie Secure default, element-nesting bound, ChannelManager eviction, two timing side channels, /ws Origin-when-cookie, de-escalation subscription teardown, two production idempotency gaps, and the scene-activate error leak) remain deferred to successor hardening slices.
claims.evidence: The hardening-audit result and the frontier hardening-audit-backlog node.

claims.statement: The change is server-only and additive: a bounded WebSocketServer factory and its wiring, plus a focused test. No protocol or Studio change and no existing behavior regresses.
claims.evidence: git diff of the CHG-0067 branch: server/src/handlers/websocket.ts, server/src/index.ts and server/tests/unit/browserWebSocketMaxPayload.test.ts.

successCriteria.statement: The browser /ws server bounds inbound frames to a finite size well below the ws 100 MiB default.
successCriteria.verification: A test asserts createBrowserWebSocketServer().options.maxPayload equals the bounded constant, which is at most the 10 MiB REST body limit and below the ws default.

successCriteria.statement: An over-limit inbound frame is rejected and never delivered to the application.
successCriteria.verification: A test sends a frame larger than a small configured bound and asserts the peer is closed with code 1009 and no message event fires.
The full server suite passes and the server type-check passes.

definitionOfDone.statement: CHG-0067 records the hardening audit result and fixes the high-severity /ws frame DoS before implementation, deferring the remaining findings.
definitionOfDone.evidence: Schema-valid record and deterministic governance compilation.

definitionOfDone.statement: The browser /ws server is created through a factory that sets a bounded maxPayload, wired into the boot path.
A test proves the bound is wired and that an oversized frame is rejected; the full server suite passes.
Governance, licensing, lint, type-check, focused and full tests, build, dependency audit and diff checks pass before handoff.
definitionOfDone.evidence: npm run governance:check, npm run check, npm run build, npm audit (0 vulnerabilities), ESLint, type-check and git diff --check; the accept commit is verified by its own pull-request Constitution run before merge.
